data_findings:
- The session_overview golden differed from the unwrapped screen by 1 px (one blue step, 57 vs 58) at (1108, 277), on a stat tile's gradient border. The cause is that a finished FadeTransition paints through an offscreen layer; this Flutter's Opacity and AnimatedOpacity render objects are repaint boundaries for any alpha above 0, including 255. A fade-only variant reproduced the diff. Removing the wrapper once landed removes it.
- `FocusNode.traversalDescendants` is in attach order, not screen order. The rail's slots sit in a lazily built ListView that builds during layout, so the switcher pinned below it attaches first. On a page with no focusable controls, Tab went switcher -> route scope -> switcher and never reached any of the 14 slots. Sorting by rect.top/left fixes it; two new regression tests cover Tab and Shift+Tab.
- At 900 px surface height, 14 slots (pitch 56 px) plus the AppMark (40 px plus gaps) plus the badge (68 px) overflow by about 20 px, so the last slot is half clipped. The rail golden uses 960 px.
- fl_chart's default swap animation is 150 ms and ignores reduced motion. The only fl_chart widget in lib/ is the BarChart in PerLapBarChart, and it now goes through AppMotion.duration.
- The full suite has 377 tests (about 11 s). New tests: test/app (shell 48 tests in total including 2 new focus-order tests, session_labels), test/design_system (hoverable, reduced_motion, staggered_entrance 10), test/features/session_overview_motion_test.dart.
spec_notes:
§8.x (Shell and accessibility polish), "Built in v0.11":
The shell now carries the app-wide keyboard and motion layer (§9.7.4, §9.7.6, §10). Reduced motion goes through one helper, AppMotion.duration(context, base), which returns zero when MediaQuery.disableAnimationsOf is true; every implicit animation in shared code uses it (page transitions, AsyncValueView cross-fade, Hoverable scale and ring, nav slots, the switcher popover, PerLapBarChart). Page transitions cannot change their fixed duration, so appPage's transitionsBuilder returns the bare page instead. Hoverable is the app's one tappable primitive: click cursor when onTap is set, a Tab stop with Enter/Space through ActivateIntent, button semantics, and a keyboard-only focus ring drawn as the gradient edge lighting up (GradientSquircleBorder in hairlineStrong, 3 px outside the child, 2 px wide, radius-aware). The ring sits outside the child because the selected nav slot's own lit edge is the same gradient, and on top of it the focused slot could not be told from the selected one.
The rail ends in a session badge (type code, open count, tooltip with circuit and session) that opens a glass popover listing the run's open sessions. Switch is OpenSessions.open(source), close is OpenSessions.close, and the popover offers "Open file...". Destinations carry a `ready` flag: Comparison, Technique, Car behavior and Settings render dimmed with "— coming soon" in the tooltip, and a test asserts every not-ready destination really is a FeaturePlaceholderScreen so the flag cannot go stale. Cmd/Ctrl+O opens a file and Cmd/Ctrl+1..9 jump to the first nine destinations; the shell owns them because they are chrome. StaggeredEntrance (40 ms stagger, 8 px paint-only rise, AppCurves.entrance) is applied to the Session Overview stat tiles, and steps out of the tree once the tile lands.
§14 findings:
(1) A finished FadeTransition is not free. Flutter's opacity render objects are repaint boundaries for any alpha above 0, including 255, and the resulting offscreen layer moved one pixel of the Session Overview golden by one blue step (57 vs 58). The entrance wrapper therefore drops itself when done (GlobalKey carries the child's state), which makes the final frame identical by construction.
(2) FocusNode.traversalDescendants is in attach order, not screen order. The rail's slots are in a lazily built ListView and attach after the pinned switcher, so on a page with no focusable controls (the Overview) the shell's "Tab goes to the rail's first stop" fallback picked the switcher, and the 14 slots were unreachable by Tab. The shell now orders by position (top, then left) and has tests for Tab and Shift+Tab.
(3) At 900 px window height the rail (14 slots at a 56 px pitch, the app mark, the 68 px badge area) overflows by about 20 px and the list scrolls. Focus scrolls the slot into view. A taller window or a smaller slot pitch would fit it.
(4) fl_chart's default swap animation (150 ms) ignores reduced motion; the only fl_chart in the app is the per-lap BarChart, which now takes its duration from AppMotion.
Not done: a visible overflow cue on the rail list; verification of the shortcuts and file picker in a real macOS window (widget tests use a fake import).
